plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It is widely cultivated in gardens and as a cut flower, and it thrives in cool fall temperatures when many other plants have finished flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: In Japan, the chrysanthemum is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after it. In many European countries, chrysanthemums are placed on graves around November 1 and 2 for All Saints' and All Souls' Day.

plants.name: Tagetes erecta
plants.description: A tall, bushy annual with pungent, ferny foliage and large pom-pom flowers. It is the iconic flower of Día de Muertos celebrations, when it is used to decorate altars and cemeteries across Mexico.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to first frost; peak bloom around late October to early November in central Mexico
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: According to tradition, the Aztec-descended custom holds that the bright color and strong scent of cempasúchil guide the spirits of the dead back to the world of the living along petal-strewn paths.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular flowering tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. Streets and parks turn purple during its bloom, and fallen blossoms carpet the ground.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, Argentina, and Brazil
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earned the city the nickname 'Jacaranda City,' and in parts of Australia the bloom traditionally coincided with university exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn, earlier than the common camellia. It produces delicate, slightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers with prominent golden stamens, and it is a valuable nectar source for late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and mild temperate regions
plants.funFact: Sasanqua leaves are related to those of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and in Japan the seeds of sasanqua are pressed for camellia oil, used in cooking and hair care.
